אֱלֹהִים stands in apposition to יַהְוֶה. Together they identify the single subject of וַיַּצְמַח.

name_review_base.evidence: יַהְוֶה names Yahweh, who caused the trees to grow from the ground.
אֱלֹהִים stands in apposition to יַהְוֶה. Together they identify the single subject of וַיַּצְמַח.

review.translation: [And|0] [Yahweh|1] [God|2] [had made to grow|0] [from|3] [the ground|4] [every|5] [tree|6] [{that}|7] [is pleasant|7] [to the sight|8] [and good|9] [for food|10], [and the tree of|11] [life|12] [in the middle of|13] [the garden|14], [and the tree of|15] [the knowledge of|16] [good|17] [and evil|18].

analysis.evidence: יַהְוֶה אֱלֹהִים is the subject and כָּל עֵץ (‘every tree’) is the object. The Hiphil expresses that Yahweh God caused the trees to grow, and מִן הָאֲדָמָה (‘from the ground’) identifies where they emerged.
analysis.morphology: Hiphil wayyiqtol, third person masculine singular, with prefixed וַ־.
analysis.sense: to cause plants to grow from the ground

analysis.evidence: יַהְוֶה אֱלֹהִים is the subject of וַיַּצְמַח (“caused to grow”). יַהְוֶה names the God who caused the trees to grow from the ground.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew proper noun with no prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: Personal name of the God of Israel

analysis.evidence: אֱלֹהִים stands in apposition to יַהְוֶה. Together they identify the subject of the singular verb וַיַּצְמַח, “he caused to grow.”
analysis.morphology: Masculine plural common noun in the absolute state, with singular reference.

analysis.evidence: With וַיַּצְמַח “he caused to sprout,” מִן הָאֲדָמָה “out of the ground” identifies the ground as the source from which the trees grew.
analysis.morphology: Independent Hebrew preposition with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: מִן הָאֲדָמָה identifies the soil from which God caused every tree to grow (וַיַּצְמַח).
analysis.morphology: Feminine singular absolute common noun with the prefixed definite article הָ־.
analysis.sense: the ground that is tilled; soil

analysis.evidence: כָּל precedes the indefinite singular עֵץ in כָּל עֵץ נֶחְמָד לְמַרְאֶה וְטוֹב לְמַאֲכָל, meaning “every tree pleasant to the sight and good for food.” It quantifies the trees that meet that description.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular noun in the construct state, with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: כָּל עֵץ means “every tree.” God causes each tree to grow from the ground, and נֶחְמָד לְמַרְאֶה וְטוֹב לְמַאֲכָל describes it as pleasing to the eye and good for food.
analysis.morphology: Common noun, masculine singular absolute, without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: נֶחְמָד agrees with עֵץ ‘tree’. The parallel phrases נֶחְמָד לְמַרְאֶה ‘pleasing to the eye’ and טוֹב לְמַאֲכָל ‘good for food’ describe the tree’s visual appeal and its value as food.
analysis.morphology: Niphal participle, masculine singular absolute, used attributively

analysis.evidence: נֶחְמָד לְמַרְאֶה describes each tree as pleasing to the eye. The parallel וְטוֹב לְמַאֲכָל describes it as good for food. In each phrase, לְ marks the respect in which the tree has the stated quality.
analysis.morphology: Preposition לְ prefixed to a masculine singular absolute noun.
analysis.sense: appearance of a thing, how it looks

analysis.evidence: טוֹב agrees with עֵץ, and וְ joins it to נֶחְמָד. The following word לְמַאֲכָל supplies “for food” and specifies the use for which the tree is good.
analysis.morphology: Conjunction וְ prefixed to a masculine singular absolute adjective.
analysis.sense: good in quality, fine, fit for use

analysis.evidence: The verse describes each tree as נֶחְמָד לְמַרְאֶה, “pleasing to the sight,” and טוֹב לְמַאֲכָל, “good for food.” The second phrase describes the tree’s suitability for eating.
analysis.morphology: Preposition לְ prefixed to a masculine singular absolute noun.

analysis.evidence: וְעֵץ הַחַיִּים means “and the tree of life.” The definite noun הַחַיִּים completes the construct phrase, and בְּתוֹךְ הַגָּן locates the tree in the middle of the garden.
analysis.morphology: Conjunction וְ prefixed to a masculine singular noun in the construct state.

analysis.evidence: In וְעֵץ הַחַיִּים, “and the tree of life,” הַחַיִּים completes the construct phrase and names the quality associated with the tree, just as הַדַּעַת names knowledge in the parallel phrase וְעֵץ הַדַּעַת.
analysis.morphology: Masculine plural noun in the absolute state with the prefixed definite article הַ־. The plural form has an abstract singular meaning.

draft.change: Assign this occurrence to the existing tavek-middle sense in tavek and clarify the construct phrase in its Gen.2.9 evidence note.
draft.definition: The middle of a place. With prefixed בְּ and a following place name or noun, the phrase locates something in the middle of that place.
draft.evidence: In Gen.2.9, עֵץ הַחַיִּים בְּתוֹךְ הַגָּן locates the tree of life relative to the garden. The construct form תוֹךְ takes הַגָּן as its complement.

analysis.evidence: Gen.2.9 places בְּתוֹךְ הַגָּן immediately after עֵץ הַחַיִּים. The phrase locates the tree of life in the middle of the garden. הַגָּן supplies the place whose middle is meant.
analysis.morphology: Prefixed preposition בְּ ‘in’ + תוֹךְ, masculine singular construct noun, followed by הַגָּן ‘the garden’. The final ךְ belongs to the noun. There is no pronominal suffix.

analysis.evidence: בְּתוֹךְ הַגָּן means “in the midst of the garden.” It locates the tree of life within the garden where God caused trees to grow.
analysis.morphology: Common noun of common gender, singular absolute, with the prefixed definite article הַ־.

analysis.evidence: וְעֵץ הַדַּעַת טוֹב וָרָע means “and the tree of the knowledge of good and evil.” The following הַדַּעַת completes the construct phrase, parallel to וְעֵץ הַחַיִּים, “and the tree of life.”
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular construct noun with prefixed conjunction וְ.

analysis.evidence: In וְעֵץ הַדַּעַת טוֹב וָרָע, הַדַּעַת names the knowledge associated with the tree. The following words טוֹב וָרָע specify what is known, good and evil.
analysis.morphology: Feminine singular absolute noun with the prefixed definite article הַ־.
analysis.sense: the knowledge of good and evil

analysis.evidence: In עֵץ הַדַּעַת טוֹב וָרָע, “the tree of the knowledge of good and evil,” טוֹב is paired with רָע. Together they name what is known.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular absolute adjective used substantivally.
analysis.sense: good (and evil): to know, discern or choose

analysis.evidence: In עֵץ הַדַּעַת טוֹב וָרָע, “the tree of the knowledge of good and evil,” טוֹב and רָע name what is known. This substantival use of רָע as the counterpart of טוֹב matches the noun entry’s paired sense.
analysis.morphology: The conjunction וָ־ joins טוֹב to רָע, the pausal form of רַע, a masculine singular absolute adjective used substantivally.
